svg.title: Figure 2 · Where the hazards sit on the risk matrix
svg.text: Figure 2 · Where the hazards sit on the risk matrix
Each hazard's initial risk (dashed) and its target after planned mitigation (solid) on the MIL-STD-882E Table III matrix.
Arrows show the planned reduction; none is verified or accepted.
Rotor start while UAV is retained or a person is at the …
False retained state releases UAV under motion
UAV launch or recovery outside the safe envelope
Unintended leg motion during pilot ingress or egress
Uncontrolled vertical drop of the cockpit on loss of leg …
Battery thermal runaway near the pilot station
Fuel leak and fire at the engine-generator
Protective stop does not reach a safe state
Stale or lost feedback causes runaway motion
Walker tip-over or fall with pilot aboard
Generated by tools/readme/build_readme.py. Preliminary judgements on a concept with no selected hardware; a hazard is accepted only by a recorded human review (rule R13).

g.text: Terms: 1A–4F = risk assessment code, severity 1–4 plus probability A–F (e.g. 1C) · DoD = US Department of Defense · F-nnn = system function in the item definition · HAZ-nnn = hazard record
(safety/hazards/HAZ-xxx-nnn.yaml) · MIL-STD-882E = US DoD Standard Practice for System Safety (11 May 2012, base edition) · R01 … = validator rule in tools/pdac (R13 = only a named human
review accepts anything) · UAV = uncrewed aerial vehicle (drone) · US = United States
